# Reconcile every open item against the base branch every few packages
## Intent

Closing an item in the run that resolves it is the main way open items
close, but it misses things: an item resolved in passing by a package that
never listed it, the issues opened before any of this existed, and the
deviations that wait for a person. Every few packages, and once at the end,
the loop reconciles every open item against the base branch. A session does
the part that needs judgement: it classifies the older issues and decides
whether each closing condition now holds. `specrun` does the rest by rule: it
chooses which issues the session may adopt, settles the deviations a person
has labelled, and checks what the session left. The list of open items stays
at most a few hours out of date, and every item on it has a path to closed.

## Goals

- **A reconcile every few packages.** After every `--reconcile-every`
  (default 5) landed packages, and once more when every package is done,
  `specrun` runs a reconcile step.
- **Older issues are adopted.** An open issue with no `af:` label whose
  title starts with `<NN_name>:` of a package under the spec root is handed
  to the session, which gives it a kind, its origin, the package it awaits
  and a severity. No other issue is ever handed over.
- **Resolved items are closed.** For every open `af:*` issue the session
  decides whether the condition in its "What closes it" holds on the base
  branch, and closes those that hold, with evidence. It changes no code.
- **A person settles a deviation with one label.** `af:accepted` closes it
  at the next reconcile; `af:rejected` turns it into a `correctness` defect.
  A deviation with neither stays open and is listed, oldest first.
- **The session is checked.** After it, `specrun` verifies that the
  repository is as it was and applies every label rule again.

## Non-goals

- **Repairs.** The repair queue that is built after each reconcile, and the
  repair sessions, are `specrun_repair`. Until then a rejected deviation
  becomes a defect that waits.
- **Editing a spec.** Accepting a deviation edits no package: the ADR and
  the closed issue are the record.
- **Touching a person's issues.** An issue whose title does not match a
  package is never handed to a session, labelled, commented on or closed.

## Background

`22_open_items_read_back` has the run that resolves an item close it, and
`specrun` relabel what awaits a finished package. What still slips through,
from the measured repository: 15 issues resolved in part by later packages,
which no single run could close; 46 issues opened before kinds existed, all
titled `<NN_name>: <what is missing>` with a body that says what is missing,
why, the evidence and what closes it; and deviations, which are decided and
recorded in an ADR but need a person's acceptance.

`specrun` (`20_specrun_driver`) has one kind of step, implementing a
package, and a state file with the steps done and the step running. Its
label rules are functions from the issues to a list of changes
(`21_open_item_labels`). af-impl takes a package as its argument and has no
other mode.

## Requirements

### 1. When a reconcile runs

A reconcile is a step of the loop. It runs after every `--reconcile-every`
landed packages (default 5), and once more when every package is done,
unless a reconcile was the last step and no package landed since. The count
of packages since the last reconcile is in the state file, so it survives a
restart. `--reconcile-every 0` leaves only the reconcile at the end. A
reconcile step recorded as running when `specrun` starts is run again.

### 2. What `specrun` hands to the session

Before the session, `specrun` selects the issues to adopt: open issues that
carry no label starting with `af:` and whose title starts with `<NN_name>:`,
where `NN_name` is the directory name of a package under the spec root or
its archive. It writes them (number, title, URL, the package) to
`<step>-adopt.json` in the log directory and starts
`claude -p "/af-impl --reconcile <adopt file> --report <report file>"` with
the flags of every session. The report file is `<step>-report.md` in the log
directory. The stall rule applies.

### 3. What the session does (af-impl text)

`/af-impl --reconcile` does only what needs a model.

**Adopting.** For each issue in the adopt file it reads the body and
assigns its kind, `af:from-<NN>`, `af:awaits-<NN>` when it awaits a package,
and a severity when it is a defect, adding those labels with a comment
saying the issue was adopted and why it got that kind. An issue whose kind
the body does not settle is labelled `af:deviation`, so a person decides it.
It adopts no issue that is not in the file.

**Checking closing conditions.** For every open `af:*` issue it decides
whether the condition in "What closes it" holds on the base branch, and
closes those that hold, with evidence (`file:line`, a test). It changes no
code, creates no branch and commits nothing.

**The report.** It writes Markdown to the report file: what it adopted, what
it closed, and the rest by kind and severity, deviations oldest first.

### 4. What `specrun` does after the session

It checks that the base branch is checked out, the tree is clean and `HEAD`
is where it was; a session that changed the repository stops the loop. A
missing report is a warning. Then, by rule, each change with a comment that
names the rule and the commit of the base branch:

- **Unsettled adoptions.** An issue from the adopt file that is still open
  and still has no kind gets `af:deviation` and `af:from-<NN>`.
- **The label rules** of the earlier packages run again over every open
  `af:` issue.
- **Accepted deviations.** An open issue with `af:deviation` and
  `af:accepted` is closed, with a comment naming the ADR the issue cites.
- **Rejected deviations.** One with `af:deviation` and `af:rejected` loses
  both labels and gets `af:defect` and `af:severity-correctness`, with a
  comment saying a person rejected the deviation.
- An issue with both `af:accepted` and `af:rejected` is left alone, with a
  warning.

The ledger line of a reconcile holds the numbers adopted, closed and
settled; the result and stderr list the open deviations with neither label,
oldest first.

### 5. The dry run

`specrun --dry-run` says when the next step is a reconcile, lists the
issues it would hand over for adoption, and adds the deviation changes to
what the label rules would change.

## Design Decisions

1. **A model runs only where judgement is needed** (PRD decision 22).
   Selecting by title, settling labelled deviations and checking the
   session follow from labels and git; classifying an issue from its prose
   and deciding whether a closing condition holds do not.
2. **Older issues are adopted by their title, and only by their title** (PRD
   decision 20). The title keeps the reconcile away from every issue a
   person opened; `deviation` puts an unclear one in front of a person.
3. **A person settles a deviation where it is tracked, with a label** (PRD
   decision 19). Accepting needs no spec edit; rejecting makes an ordinary
   defect.
4. **Deviations are listed, not stopped on** (PRD decision 13).
5. **Reconcile every 5 packages by default** (PRD decision 15): five
   packages took 4 to 6 hours in the measured run.
6. **The adopt list and the report path are arguments of the session.** The
   PRD's `/af-impl --reconcile` leaves open how the session learns which
   issues `specrun` selected; a file it is told to read is checked the same
   way every time, and a report at a path `specrun` chose can be found.
7. **`specrun` labels what the session left unsettled.** The PRD has the
   session label an unclear issue `af:deviation`; a session that skipped one
   would leave it invisible, so the rule runs after it too.
8. **The reconcile session must not move `HEAD`.** It changes no code, so a
   commit on the base branch is a session that did something else.
9. **Both `af:accepted` and `af:rejected` is nobody's decision.** The issue
   stays as it is and the warning names it.
10. **No final reconcile right after a reconcile.** When the last package
    happens to land on a multiple of `--reconcile-every`, one reconcile
    serves as both.
11. **`--reconcile-every 0` keeps the final reconcile.** Nothing in this
    plan is switched off entirely by a default or by zero.

## Dependencies

- `22_open_items_read_back` (active): the label rules that run again, the
  closing of items by af-impl and the dry run's `would_change`.
- `aflib/issuex` for listing, labelling, commenting and closing
  (`Client.CloseIssue(ctx, ref IssueRef, comment string) error`, read in a
  checkout at commit `6b70ef7`); the `issue` command, which the session
  uses.
- The af-impl skill (`skills/af-impl`), which gains the `--reconcile` mode.

## Glossary

- **reconcile**: one step of the loop that brings every open item in line
  with the base branch: a session for the judgement, rules for the rest.
- **adopting**: giving an issue opened before the label scheme its kind and
  labels.
- **settling**: a person deciding a deviation with `af:accepted` or
  `af:rejected`.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Run a reconcile every few packages and at the end

**Rationale:** A list that is only corrected at the end is out of date for the whole run.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN the number of packages landed since the last reconcile reaches `--reconcile-every`, 5 when the flag is absent, THE specrun SHALL run a reconcile step before the next package
   → the reconcile's session starts after that package's landing and before the next package's session; the count in the state file returns to 0
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
   ```
   in internal/specrun/reconcile_test.go (new), a table over --reconcile-every {1, 2, 5} with five open packages: assert the order of the sessions started, by their prompts: with 2 -> 01, 02, reconcile, 03, 04, reconcile, 05, reconcile; with 5 -> five packages then one reconcile; with 1 -> a reconcile after each and none added at the end
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN every package is done and a package has landed since the last reconcile, or no reconcile is recorded in the ledger, THE specrun SHALL run one reconcile step before ending
   → the last session of the run is a reconcile; when the last step was a reconcile and no package landed since, no session starts and the run ends with `all_done`
   Check: same as REQ-1.1
1. [REQ-1.3] WHERE `--reconcile-every` is given, THE specrun SHALL take the number of packages between reconciles from it, `0` meaning only the reconcile at the end, with `SPECRUN_RECONCILE_EVERY` as its default when set
   → a negative number or a value that is no integer is a usage error with exit code 2 naming the flag or the variable; with `0` and five packages the only reconcile is the last session
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/specrun/flags_test.go, beside the existing flag tables: {absent -> 5; 3 -> 3; 0 -> 0; SPECRUN_RECONCILE_EVERY=2 -> 2; -1 -> exit code 2; 'often' -> exit code 2}; in internal/specrun/reconcile_test.go one case with 0 and five packages: the session order is the five packages, then reconcile
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN `specrun` is started and its state records the count of packages since the last reconcile, or a reconcile step as running, THE specrun SHALL continue from that count, and run a reconcile recorded as running again
   → with `--reconcile-every 2`, one package landed before the restart and one after it, the reconcile follows the second; a running reconcile is the first session after the restart
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
   ```
   in internal/specrun/reconcile_test.go: run --max 1 --reconcile-every 2, then run --max 1 --reconcile-every 2: assert the second run's sessions are [02, reconcile]; with a state file naming a reconcile as running: assert the first session's prompt starts '/af-impl --reconcile'
   ```

### REQ-2: Hand the session the issues it may adopt, and nothing else

**Rationale:** A reconcile that could touch any issue would sooner or later relabel one a person opened.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a reconcile step starts, THE specrun SHALL select the open issues that carry no label starting with `af:` and whose title starts with the directory name of a package under the spec root or its archive followed by a colon, write them to `<step>-adopt.json` in the log directory, and start the session
   → the file is a JSON array of `{number, title, url, package}`, `[]` when none is selected; the session's prompt is `/af-impl --reconcile <adopt file> --report <log dir>/<step>-report.md`, with the flags, the stall rule and the stream files of every session
   Check: integration

   ```
   in internal/specrun/reconcile_test.go, with packages 01_alpha, 02_beta and an archived 00_zero, a table over open issues: {'01_alpha: no caller', no label -> selected with package 01_alpha; '00_zero: gap', label bug -> selected; '01_alpha: x', label af:defect -> not; 'alpha: y' -> not; '01_alphabet: z' -> not; '09_none: q' -> not; 'Crash on start' -> not; a closed '02_beta: w' -> not}: assert the adopt file holds exactly the two selected entries; assert the fake claude's prompt names that file and a report path in the log directory; assert a .jsonl stream file exists for the step
   ```

   → exit code 1; `result.stopped.reason` names the check; the ledger line has outcome `stopped`; no rule is applied to the forge and no further session starts

1. [REQ-2.3] IF the reconcile session ends and the report file does not exist, THEN THE specrun SHALL warn and go on
   → `warnings` holds one `reconcile_report_missing` entry naming the path; the rules run and the ledger line has outcome `reconciled`

### REQ-3: Settle by rule what needs no judgement, after the session

**Rationale:** Labels, the dependency graph and git decide these; a rule applies them the same way every time, at no model cost.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a reconcile session has passed its checks and an issue from the adopt file is still open with no kind label, THE specrun SHALL add `af:deviation` and `af:from-<NN>` of the package its title names, and comment on it
   → the issue carries both labels and one comment naming the rule `adoption-unsettled` and the commit of the base branch; an adopted issue that has a kind is left to the other label rules
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
   ```
   in internal/specrun/reconcile_test.go: a fake session that labels one of two adopt-file issues af:defect, af:severity-minor, af:from-01 and leaves the other: assert the other carries af:deviation and af:from-01 and a comment containing 'adoption-unsettled'; assert the first got no write from specrun
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN a reconcile session has passed its checks and an open issue carries `af:deviation` and `af:accepted` and not `af:rejected`, THE specrun SHALL close the issue with a comment naming the ADR the issue cites
   → the issue is closed; the comment names the rule `deviation-accepted`, the commit of the base branch and the first path `docs/adr/<file>.md` in the issue's body, or says that the issue cites no ADR
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
   ```
   in internal/specrun/reconcile_test.go, a table over open issues at a reconcile: {af:deviation + af:accepted, body citing docs/adr/07-x.md -> closed, comment contains that path; the same with no ADR in the body -> closed, comment says none is cited; af:deviation + af:rejected -> open, labels af:defect and af:severity-correctness, neither af:deviation nor af:rejected, comment contains 'deviation-rejected'; af:deviation alone -> no write; af:deviation + af:accepted + af:rejected -> no write and a deviation_conflict warning naming it; af:defect + af:accepted -> no write}: assert the state, labels and comments of each
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN a reconcile session has passed its checks and an open issue carries `af:deviation` and `af:rejected` and not `af:accepted`, THE specrun SHALL remove `af:deviation` and `af:rejected`, add `af:defect` and `af:severity-correctness`, and comment that a person rejected the deviation
   → the issue is open with `af:defect`, `af:severity-correctness` and its `af:from-<NN>`; the comment names the rule `deviation-rejected` and the commit of the base branch
   Check: same as REQ-3.2
1. [REQ-3.4] IF an open issue carries `af:accepted` and `af:rejected` together, THEN THE specrun SHALL leave the issue as it is and warn
   → the forge records no write for it; `warnings` holds one `deviation_conflict` entry naming the issue
   Check: same as REQ-3.2
1. [REQ-3.5] WHEN the rules of a reconcile have been applied, THE specrun SHALL apply the label rules `incomplete-labels` and `awaits-finished` to every open `af:` issue, write the ledger line, and list the open deviations that carry neither `af:accepted` nor `af:rejected`, oldest first
   → the ledger line has kind `reconcile`, outcome `reconciled` and the numbers `adopted`, `closed` and `settled`: issues from the adopt file that now carry a kind, issues open before the step and closed after it, and deviations accepted or rejected; `result.open_deviations` lists number, title, URL and creation time, oldest first, and stderr prints the same
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
   ```
   in internal/specrun/reconcile_test.go: a fake session that adopts two issues and closes one af:awaits issue, with one accepted deviation and three plain deviations created on different days, and one af:awaits issue toward a finished package: assert last(ledger) has kind 'reconcile', outcome 'reconciled', adopted 2, closed 2, settled 1; assert numbers(result.open_deviations) are in creation order; assert the af:awaits issue was relabelled by awaits-finished
   ```

### REQ-4: Show the reconcile in a dry run

**Rationale:** The reconcile writes to many issues at once; a person should be able to see the list first.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHERE `--dry-run` is given and a forge client can be made, THE specrun SHALL say when the next step is a reconcile, list the issues it would hand over for adoption, and add the deviation changes to what the label rules would change
   → `result.next_step.kind` is `reconcile` when one is due; `result.would_adopt` lists the selected issues; `result.would_change` holds an entry with rule `deviation-accepted` or `deviation-rejected` for each labelled deviation; the forge records no write and no file is written
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
   ```
   in internal/specrun/reconcile_test.go: with a state file counting 5 packages since the last reconcile, one adoptable issue, one accepted and one rejected deviation: run --dry-run; assert next_step.kind == 'reconcile', len(would_adopt) == 1, the two rules among would_change, no forge write, no adopt file and no session
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: specrun reconciles after a package: an old issue is adopted, a resolved one closed, an accepted deviation settled

1. **operator** adds `af:accepted` to a deviation issue and runs `specrun --reconcile-every 1`
2. **specrun** runs the session for the next package and checks the landing
3. **specrun** starts a reconcile: selects the unlabelled issue titled after a package, writes the adopt file and starts the reconcile session
4. **session** labels the adopted issue with its kind and origin, closes an issue whose closing condition holds on the base branch, and writes the report
5. **specrun** checks that the repository is as it was, applies the label rules, closes the accepted deviation with a comment naming its ADR
6. **specrun** writes the reconcile's ledger line and lists the deviations still open

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** specrun's Main, afspec, git, the fake claude as a real process, the reconcile rules against the in-memory issuex client, the adopt file, the report and the ledger on disk

**Setup:**

- the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
- one open package; on the forge an unlabelled open issue '00_zero: no caller', an open af:awaits issue, an open af:deviation + af:accepted issue citing docs/adr/03-x.md, and an open af:deviation issue; a fake reconcile session that labels the first, closes the second and writes the report

**End state:**

- the sessions started are the package, then a reconcile whose prompt names the adopt file and the report
- the adopted issue carries the kind the session gave it and got no write from specrun
- the accepted deviation is closed with a comment containing docs/adr/03-x.md
- the ledger's last line is a reconcile with adopted 1, closed 2, settled 1
- the result lists one open deviation and exit code is 0

**Pseudocode:**

```
in cmd/specrun/main_test.go, beside the existing end-to-end tests: code = Main(['--reconcile-every', '1']); assert code == 0; assert prompts == ['/af-impl .specs/01_…', '/af-impl --reconcile … --report …']; assert the adopt file lists one issue; assert state(accepted deviation) == 'closed'; l = last(ledger); assert l.kind == 'reconcile' and l.adopted == 1 and l.closed == 2 and l.settled == 1; assert len(env.result.open_deviations) == 1
```

- 3.4 Checking closing conditions, in that file: list every open af:* issue; for each decide whether the condition in 'What closes it' holds on the base branch; close those that hold with `issue <ref> --close --body`, the comment giving the evidence as file and line and a test; change no code, create no branch and commit nothing
- 3.5 The report, in that file: Markdown written to the report path, listing what was adopted with the kind given, what was closed with its evidence, and the rest by kind and severity, deviations oldest first
- 3.6 In SKILL.md name the mode in the argument hint and in §1, and extend the last rule of *Never*: in a reconcile af-impl may label the issues of the adopt file; keep the rendered body under the ceiling `make skills-check` enforces

- `cmd/specrun/main_test.go`
